findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE changed from 4 to 3, breaking existing automation
findings.body: This PR redefines RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and repurposes 4 as FEATURE_DISABLED. The update-compatibility command is already shipped (as preview) and the docs explicitly tell users to build automation around the exit codes ('consumers... should rely only on the exit code of the check command'). Any existing script or pipeline that treats exit code 4 as 'recreate upgrade required' will silently misbehave after this change: a real recreate situation now returns 3 (which their script may treat as an unknown/unexpected error, or worse, ignore), and a feature-disabled run returns 4, which old scripts would interpret as 'shut down the deployment for a recreate upgrade' even though nothing is actually incompatible. Even for a preview feature, silently remapping an already-documented contract value warrants an explicit release note / migration note, or choosing a new unused code for FEATURE_DISABLED instead of renumbering.

findings.title: Caution claims the Operator fails without rolling-updates feature, contradicting default-strategy behavior
findings.body: The new CAUTION block states: 'While on preview stage, the feature rolling-updates must be enabled. Otherwise, the Keycloak Operator will fail.' However, the default behavior (update strategy not set) intentionally mimics Keycloak 26.1 and works without the feature: the modified UpgradeTest.createInitialDeployment only enables the rolling-updates feature when an explicit update strategy is configured, and the null-strategy parameterized runs (testImageChange / testCacheMaxCount) deploy and roll successfully without the feature. As written, the doc tells users the operator will break unless they enable a preview feature, which is incorrect for anyone not using spec.update.strategy and will cause unnecessary enablement of a preview feature (or panic). The caution should be scoped to 'when spec.update.strategy is set' or reworded.

findings.title: testFeatureNotEnabled does not assert exit code 4
findings.body: The new test for the feature-disabled path only asserts the error message text. The PR introduces a dedicated exit code (CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED = 4) and documents it in update-compatibility.adoc as part of the scriptable contract, but no test verifies that the metadata/check commands actually exit with code 4 when the feature is disabled (nor that the check command exits with 3 on incompatibility in testWrongVersions). A regression that returns code 0 or the generic error code 1 in these paths would go unnoticed while breaking consumers that rely on the documented exit codes.
